There have been some upstream API changes (like splitting `screen_luminance` into `auto_adjust_reference_luminance` and `auto_adjust_maximum_luminance`) which this PR has not been updated to cover. Do you plan on updating this PR once the upstream one has been merged? Asking because some things like high/low precision have different behaviour on wayland than it did on windows (on windows low precision is faster, on wayland high precision is faster) so mac might have even more different behaviour than either of them. Windows HDR on vulkan is broadly broken but it seems you've verified than on mac things work well?

The primary useful point of data would be which of high/low precision is faster on macos (and that they both work, on wayland they used to not work until changes were made to the godot vulkan driver).

@Calinou Thanks for testing this on Mac. There's a *chance* that some of this is from old bugs that have since been since been fixed (this hasn't been rebased in a while) but most likely there's some very important performance considerations around high/low precision on mac that would be worth bringing up with allenwp.

As for the hue shifts hopefully it's just a bug in the metal implemtation (the colorspaces chosen in metal say something about P3 which seems strange to me) but if there's also a bug in the vulkan implementation it's good to have caught it here.

> Do you plan on updating this PR once the upstream one has been merged?

@ArchercatNEO absolutely! Just waiting for the upstream PR to stabilise and merge and I'll rework this PR. I'm very excited to add EDR support for Apple.
@Calinou identified a bug in how the MetalFX spatial shader is configured, that has been fixed in #109406

> Running the test project. I've tested each run at least twice as many of the results are unexpected, namely HDR off being slower than HDR on (with high precision disabled).

I wonder if you would observe the same if you target a non-HDR display? Pure speculation, but is it possible that Apple's rendering / compositing pipeline on the MacBook Pro's built-in display is always HDR, so SDR content must be converted?

Generally, I've seen all Metal literature indicate the default pixel format it BGRA8 for views.
I think you can set the colorspace of the display to be SDR-only.

However, I am getting HDR output when previewing the project via the 2D Tab in the editor. I'm not really sure why this is the case.

> Tried out the PR on my M1 Pro MacBook Pro. Not getting any HDR output when running @allenwp's test project, but I assume this is intended at this moment, as macOS embedded display driver support isn't added yet.

Correct – I'm working on that now. You should be able to launch @allenwp's project (no `--editor`) and it will work

> However, I am getting HDR output when previewing the project via the 2D Tab in the editor. I'm not really sure why this is the case.

That is the expected behaviour

@allenwp all you requested updates are done – one outstanding question for when error message to display when setting linear luminance scale.

I'm also going to see if the OS event for display property updates includes both `maximumExtendedDynamicRangeColorComponentValue` and `maximumPotentialExtendedDynamicRangeColorComponentValue`, as that will be cleaner if I can directly respond to those.

Latest commits 

- fix the issues raised by @allenwp
  - replicated in the Apple Embedded display driver
- ensure that on iOS devices update the EDR values real-time as they change (due to ambient light or brightness changes)


Tested:

- ✅ MacBook Pro
- ✅ iPhone 
- ✅ Apple Vision Pro

Hmm. I hadn't realized that Vulkan HDR output would be possible on Mac OS. This updated version of the PR appears to work correctly with Metal, but luminance values are wrong with Vulkan.

If we're in a rush to get this in a mergable state ASAP, we could disable Vulkan HDR output support on Mac OS, like it is on Windows. Or if we're not in a rush we can carefully get both working well.

> It looks like there is significant refactoring of the various display servers on Apple's platforms. Should those refactors be done in another PR so this one can focus on the HDR related changes?

I have removed the field access changes to godot_view_apple_embedded.mm; the remaining changes are related to HDR support.

> but luminance values are wrong with Vulkan.

Could you clarify why they are wrong with Vulkan?

> Hmm. I hadn't realized that Vulkan HDR output would be possible on Mac OS. This updated version of the PR appears to work correctly with Metal, but luminance values are wrong with Vulkan.

If the correct values are always pushed down into the rendering context (as opposed to being calculated within the context) we should be able to get Vulkan and Metal looking the same.

I think we should try to do as little calculation within the renderers as possible, making sure the display servers are in charge of computing the correct HDR values and telling the renderer what to do.

Related to that, maybe we should also implement `linear_luminance_scale` within the context so the display servers can ensure its value is the same as `reference_luminance`?

> Related to that, maybe we should also implement `linear_luminance_scale` within the context so the display servers can ensure its value is the same as `reference_luminance`?

My suspicion, based purely on conjecture from doing a quick test on my Macbook, is that `linear_luminance_scale` must equal **current** reference luminance for Metal and always equal `100.0` for Vulkan. This needs testing and confirmation, I'm really just taking a guess here at what Vulkan needs.

> > but luminance values are wrong with Vulkan.
> 
> Could you clarify why they are wrong with Vulkan?

Probably easiest if you just open my test project and compare what things look like with a high brightness with metal and a high brightness with vulkan. You'll notice that Vulkan is too bright. My suspicion is that the `linear_luminance_scale` must equal `100.0` for Vulkan and must equal the current reference luminance for Metal -- this explains why things look good in Vulkan when the user changes their screen brightness to 100 nits, but then becomes too bright when they increase their brightness.
@allenwp I'd advocate that we disable Vulkan HDR support to move this PR forward and then evaluate support in a separate set of PRs, in conjunction with Windows.

> @allenwp I'd advocate that we disable Vulkan HDR support to move this PR forward and then evaluate support in a separate set of PRs, in conjunction with Windows.

Sounds good. Should be relatively easy to add Vulkan support to Apple devices, but also sounds like it would just delay things for little benefit, given Metal is the default driver for Apple devices.

> in conjunction with Windows.

Also, for clarity, Vulkan HDR output should never be added to Windows. The reason it's not supported on Windows is simply because Windows GPU drivers do not correctly support Vulkan swapchains for HDR. Unless we change the Vulkan driver to use a DXGI swapchain, this is outside of our control and therefore we can never support it.
@Calinou I was validating embedded support and it should work in all scenarios. I will check specifically embedding _in the editor window_, as I was testing the pop out version mostly.

>     * HDR output isn't supported when using the embedded game window on macOS, presumably since the window uses an IPC approach to get the framebuffer data from the game process (instead of the fake windowing approach used on Windows and Linux/X11). This can be left for a future PR, but we should make sure this is documented in the manual as it's likely going to cause confusion at first.

This is just a bug in this PR. I can reproduce that HDR output doesn't work when you first launch the game with a project that has request_hdr_output on. But if you move that embedded game window between screens with a multi-screen setup, it will fix the bug and HDR output will work correctly in the embedded game window.

> We should surface the tonemapper and glow Soft Light warnings as node configuration warnings in the WorldEnvironment node when HDR is enabled in the project settings, so that they're more easily noticed. I can implement this in a future PR.

Yeah, sounds good. I'll add this as a note to the tracker list.

> In the above demo, AgX tonemapping won't increase the dynamic range, while it does in my [HDR test project](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/21170122/test-hdr.zip). Toggling HDR output will only change how much glow appears, but it won't make the red sphere or the ground actually brighter in the Sponza scene. I'm not sure if this is a demo issue.

Would be good to know if this happens with the Windows PR as well...

I have found a bug that `NSApplicationDidChangeScreenParametersNotification` are not posted in the embedded game process (as it isn't a normal NSApp), so I will have to forward them from the parent window instead. I am still seeing HDR content displayed, but it would not be updated correctly.

Expect a commit to follow to address that.

The latest commit should resolve embedded window issues. The root cause was twofold:

1. We can't subscribed to `NSApplicationDidChangeScreenParametersNotification` in the embedded process, as it doesn't raise events (probably because it isn't a windowed `NSApplication`
2. The NSScreen EDR values were not changing in response to brightness or ambient light changes in the embedded process, likely for the same reason as 1.

To resolve this, I now push the EDR values from the parent process, like a few of the other DisplayServer values.

> @stuartcarnie You might want to take a look at how the Android HDR PR handles passing down the correct luminance values into the renderer: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/101977/changes#diff-8bb68587d6789e5c7c59875648c86283c32e68a3ff0d78388e39a34ef144609aR458
> 
> I think both Android and macOS/iOS handle HDR similarly where they both use an EDR scheme. Since the Android implementation works well with Vulkan, I'm wondering if a similar approach will help this PR get Vulkan working.
> 
> At the end of the day, neither renderer really understands nits, everything gets squashed down to signal values that are interpreted by the graphics driver. Hopefully MoltenVK isn't doing any funny conversions to that value.

Sure thing!

I'd like to do that in a separate PR, so as to not make any further changes to this for @allenwp, and ideally to get this in to the first dev release for users to start testing. It should be a relatively small follow-up PR, and we can focus on testing Vulkan independently.

Thanks for your work on this, Stuart! When I toggle HDR output off on my external display, it correctly disables HDR at the system level and my monitor shows that it's receiving an SDR signal, but my Godot window still thinks that HDR output is supported by the window: Before (system HDR on) | After (system HDR off) --|-- | Is this something you can reproduce @stuartcarnie or is this something that you need me to debug and fix? **Edit:** Hmm. It seems this bug is specific to using the /System/Library/ColorSync/Profiles/ITU-2020.icc colour profile. The bug doesn't reproduce when I use the default colour profile of my monitor. So maybe this is a macOS bug?? Also, I noticed that the HDR code between (at least) `DisplayServerMacOSBase` and `DisplayServerAppleEmbedded` does not match. Of specific issue are things like [comments](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/106814/changes#diff-02e997eae7e3917de38375685775ae983ff69c3776158596f36058d7771ae3b4R886) and [warnings](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/106814/changes#diff-02e997eae7e3917de38375685775ae983ff69c3776158596f36058d7771ae3b4R882). These should be identical copy-and-pastes of each other and kept in sync. Although I haven't tested iOS yet, from looking at the code in `DisplayServerAppleEmbedded`, it appears that it is possible to change the max luminance. I don't know of a normal use case where this functionality is required for iOS, so I believe that the max luminance functions in `DisplayServerAppleEmbedded` should behave similar to the reference luminance functions: max luminance should always be `-1.0` and it should throw a warning when the user tries to set it: `Manually setting max luminance is not supported on iOS devices as they provide accurate max luminance values for their built-in screens.` For comparison, macOS requires the "manual max luminance" feature because the player may connect an external HDR screen that incorrectly reports its max luminance value. In this case, the player will need an in-game setting to adjust their max luminance setting to be different than what macOS is reporting. I don't think this scenario comes up as often or at all with iOS... it's possible this might also happen when doing screen sharing to an Apple TV, for example, but I think it would be better to add this manual max later when we know it is an actual problem that needs solving. (This follows better with Godot's development approach of only solving real problems rather than hypothetical ones.)

> Edit: Hmm. It seems this bug is specific to using the /System/Library/ColorSync/Profiles/ITU-2020.icc colour profile. The bug doesn't reproduce when I use the default colour profile of my monitor. So maybe this is a macOS bug??

Yes, I think so – I also can't reproduce it normally.

@allenwp If I switch to the same `/System/Library/ColorSync/Profiles/ITU-2020.icc` profile; it remains stuck. Under default profile it correctly toggles, so I suspect there is a macOS issue that it is not publishing the event correctly, when display preferences change.

Cool, I'm glad you're seeing the same behaviour I am. I need to use this non-default Rec. BT.2020 profile with my screen because my screen only supports its native (default) colour profile when HDR is disabled. But if it's a macOS bug, then it's a macOS bug and we can't do anything about it ¯\_(ツ)_/¯

I've done some testing on my iPhone 13 Pro and this looks amazing. Thanks!

There's an issue that happens inconsistently for me. I'm mentioning it here in case you have any idea of why this might happen:

1. Turn off auto-brightness on the iPhone
2. Set brightness to around 50% (maybe a smidge higher)
3. Open my [HDR output porting test project](https://github.com/allenwp/godot-hdr-output-test-project)
4. Note that the max luminance is correctly 800 nits and reference luminance is around 100 nits, giving a max linear value of 8.0
5. Turn off "request HDR output" toggle switch in the "player facing in-game settings" section of the app
6. Tap save to save these player settings
7. Restart the game
8. Note that the game is correctly in SDR mode because it read the player setting
9. Turn on HDR output using the toggle switch
10. **Problem:** max linear value is limited to around 1.2 instead of 8.0 and reference luminance is around 670 nits instead of 100. Max luminance is correctly 800 nits
11. Adjust system brightness slightly
12. Note that the problem is resolved and the max linear value and reference luminance go back to the correct values.

Unfortunately, I can't get this to happen consistently. It might be that I need to switch back and forth between apps to get it to happen...

Anyway, it smells like an iOS bug, though it's possible that there is a moment that we should be checking for HDR luminance info that we aren't. Hard to tell.


**EDIT:**

I was able to get my iPhone back into this state and determined that the issue has nothing to do with the auto brightness setting; it happens with auto brightness on or off.

Also, it seems that it is an iOS bug. My max output value stayed at 1.2 until I changed brightness no matter what I did in the Godot app. I also saw what appeared to be the same behaviour in my iPhone Photos app! I when I adjusted my screen brightness, I saw my photos properly go to the full HDR appearance and was able to tell that they were not properly showing as HDR before I adjusted the brightness.

So, all this to say, definitely an iOS bug and nothing to do with Godot.

> Hmm, odd. It doesn't compile from VSCode or the terminal but compiling within XCode works.

It might be a mismatch of Xcode and command line tools, which sometimes happens:

- Check the output of `xcode-select -p` command, if it's not `/Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer`, run `sudo xcode-select -s /Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer`.
- If it won't help, delete `/Library/Developer/CommandLineTools` and run `xcode-select --install` to reinstall command line tools.
